Scope and decision

Proceed to Run 30 only after this audit report, source update and index update have saved successfully. Final packaging is still unfinished. This audit does not mark the program complete or assess learner mastery.

The latest operating instructions, curriculum, index and source register were retrieved. The index selected Audit D. Exact-title and shorter-title searches returned no existing Audit D report, and the index had no such identity to reconcile. Fresh copies of all 48 lesson/answer artifacts and three prior audit reports were retrieved through their registered identities. All 51 resolved successfully; no missing prerequisite file or interrupted lesson save was found.

This is a cross-curriculum audit with concentrated technical review of B02/B03 and C03–C06, the material produced after Audit C. Earlier coverage is supported by the saved Audits A–C, inspection of their repairs and a fresh execution of every answer script. It is not an exhaustive new reading of every paragraph or every source. Repeating synthetic checks is reproducibility evidence, not independent empirical validation.

Findings and disposition

ID Issue or risk examined Evidence and disposition Affected material / remaining limits
D-01 F04 and its companion still labeled produced in the index despite completed review Audit C explicitly reviewed F04’s math and six answer mappings; its script passed again. Reconcile F04’s register and run-table states to audited Index-only repair. F04 content and stable identities remain unchanged
D-02 Different meanings of success across lessons might look contradictory A05 distinguishes contract-correct refusal from a supported draft; B02 bills verified supported outcomes; C03 counts timely correct serving outputs; C05 permits internal review routing; C06 explicitly returns to evidence preparation Boundaries are stated, so no text repair. Do not combine these rates as if they measured one unchanged task
D-03 Synthetic capacity checks might be mistaken for actual deadline evidence C03 explicitly excludes retrieval/network/human time from its serving-stage clock; C05 calls daily capacity an average-work planning gate; C06 calls equal adequacy provisional No correction. Arrival patterns, workload and human queues remain unmeasured
D-04 Contribution, customer value and supplier profit could be conflated B02 excludes unlisted costs from operating remainder; B03 separates customer capacity value from supplier contribution; C04 explicitly adds overhead to B03; C06 uses customer migration cost No correction. New scenario numbers do not overwrite earlier scenarios
D-05 Retry permission or a historical receipt could become fresh authority S06 and C05 require current receipt-read permission separately from fresh mutation permission; C06 read-only inference retries do not authorize business effects No correction. Sequential fixtures assume the atomic boundary and do not implement authentication or distributed recovery
D-06 Migration export count mistaken for evidence continuity C06 rejects missing revisions, corrupt bytes and equal-count replacement of a referenced revision; S02 preserves original bytes and exact historical identities No correction. A trusted manifest and actual rights/restore process remain premises
D-07 Prior audit repairs lost or overstated F03 retains the t-interval assumptions; S01 retains rate upper-bound language; S04 answers retain the warning about unreachable synthetic predicate states No regression found. Prior source reviews remain dated evidence, not a claim of fresh inspection of every source

No lesson was regenerated and no technical correction was manufactured to justify a new revision. The index reconciliation resolves a production-state inconsistency, not a mathematical defect. Newly reviewed B02/B03 and C03–C06, plus their companions, receive audited states after the audit is saved. Prior audit reports retain their own produced state as reports.

Recomputed decisions and counterexamples

Material Result checked against stated premises What would invalidate using it in deployment?
B02 Baseline variable cost 2 U/attempt, 2.5 U/success; operating remainder −300 U; first-tier break-even 1,250 cases; retry improvement to 0.85 with zero incremental contribution Unmeasured conditional retry recovery, capacity tiers, omitted labor or failed collection
B03 Customer values 360/660/900 U; bundle value 810 U; managed fee ceiling 155 below supplier recovery floor 168.33… U Different quality, rights, actual willingness to pay, or recurring support effort
C03 Initial timely counts 4/8,8/8,8/8 and useful costs 60/30/55 U; longer output makes only two replicas satisfy all eight Different phase curves, startup, unsupported output, billing or arrival distribution
C04 Initial four-hour setup cap excludes internal deployment; twelve hours permits it. Supplier remainders with added overhead are 160 and 10 U Missing authority, no operating owner, or greater maintenance/overhead
C05 Costs 1.50/2.65/1.75; review demand 1,000/4,000/400 minutes. Capacity reduction from 1,200 to 500 changes W to A Actual oversight exceeds budget, queue misses deadlines or authority gate fails
C06 Initial six-month costs 9,000/9,900/11,100 U; incumbent fee 700 makes replacement cheaper. Thresholds: fee 550, recovery three months, bundle handling 2.8 minutes Incompatible behavior, inadequate quality, export restrictions or omitted migration cost

The cross-module lesson holds: permission and feasibility are gates; cost ranking comes afterward. A cheaper model call is not necessarily a cheaper completed case. A faster component is not necessarily a better customer outcome. A reversible internal route is not payment approval. A supplier abstraction does not establish equivalent behavior. These are conclusions within the described contracts, not claims that a real deployment has passed the gates.

The numerical differences between B03 and C04 are intentional. C04 imports the customer inputs and adds 10 U monthly supplier overhead, reducing supplier six-month remainders by 60 U each. C05 changes the permitted job explicitly; C06 then explicitly returns to the earlier evidence job. No hidden cross-run authority expansion was found.

Execution and completeness record

All 24 embedded Python blocks exited successfully. Each ran in a separate process, preventing cross-file variable contamination. Tests were extracted from the freshly retrieved companions, not copied from past execution output.

Group Scripts rerun Selected coverage
F01–F04 4 Invariant/counterexamples; probability tables and losses; paired counts; vector/gradient and held-out loss calculations
S01–S06 6 Cache/translation models; publication/recovery; interleavings and receipts; quorum predicates; queue/fan-out; authority/SLO models
A01–A05 5 Splits/generalization; attention; retrieval and provenance; memory/scheduling; bounded loop and evaluation ledgers
B01–B03 3 Customer-value units; cost/retry thresholds; cohorts, payback and bundling
C01–C06 6 Effect boundaries; outcome/deadline choice; capacity; product boundary; autonomy; supplier change

For the newly audited group, executed coverage includes B02’s 1,001 success-count and 108 retry cases; B03’s 2,401 fee and 25 maintenance points; C03’s 39 length/policy and 1,206 deadline checks; C04’s 2,450 decision cases; C05’s 1,501 capacity cases and 16 guard combinations; C06’s 1,001 fee cases, 12 horizons, four export fixtures and two publication states. These counts describe finite fixtures, not real trials or full protocol state-space coverage.

Inventory checks found exactly 18 core packs, six synthesis memos and 24 matching answer companions. There are 138 numbered solution sections: six for each core and five for each synthesis. Assignment/answer coverage was checked through numbered sections, topic alignment in the newly reviewed group, and the earlier audit records for earlier groups. This is not a fresh independent marking of 138 learner responses; none exist.

All 48 relative Markdown links between lessons and companions resolve in the retrieved tree. Every registered identity used for the 51 lesson/answer/audit files resolved to its named file. The dependency map’s 18 core module references exist. Every R-number used in the retrieved artifacts is present in the source register. Fences are balanced. Native identity resolution and local-link checks do not imply that every historical external URL was crawled during this audit.

Sources were inspected on 2026-11-15. R01–R24 identities are preserved. No new source was necessary. This targeted review supplements the detailed dated passage records in Audits A–C; it does not claim all 24 sources were freshly revalidated or every historical URL is permanently available.

Remaining uncertainty and handoff

No blocking educational error was found in this scope. Open application inputs remain actual workload, sample dependence, labels and evaluator quality, authority implementation, crash/retention semantics, prices, cost allocation, staffing, rights and demand. Synthetic assertions cannot settle these. The reports consistently distinguish constructed values from observations.

Run 30 must create SDE_START_HERE.md with reading routes, consolidated notes, separate solutions, reference cards and an open-questions ledger, plus an archive or consolidated export. It must verify final links and packaging from current saved versions. Only after those deliverables and the final index have saved successfully should the program be marked complete and its automation disabled. No additional lessons or filler are needed.
